rows: Penny to quarter size hail fell in 60 to 65 mph winds in both Kermit and Wink, breaking many windows and shredding south facing building sides.
The Kermit Police Department reported hail up to two inches in diameter fell in Kermit. Coupled with high winds, the large hail broke many windows and shredded south facing building sides.
Penny to quarter size hail fell in 60 to 65 mph winds in both Kermit and Wink, breaking many windows and shredding south facing building sides.
The Automated Surface Observing System at Wink (KINK) recorded two 72 mph wind gusts, one at 5:26pm CDT, the other at 5:34pm CDT. No damage was reported at this time.
The Winkler County Sheriff's Office reported that a tree was downed by thunderstorm winds and landed on a carport. They also reported that power lines were downed around Wink.
Five inch diameter limbs were broken off trees in northeastern Winkler County.
A tree with a three foot diameter trunk was downed by thunderstorm winds.
Nickel to quarter size hail was reported in Kermit.
Nickel to golfball sized hail fell in eastern Winkler County and stripped leaves off the trees.
Golfball to baseball sized hail fell on Texas Highway 302 near the Winkler and Ector County lines.
The Automated Surface Observing System at Wink (KINK) recorded several wind gusts of 59 mph. No damage was reported.
A brief tornado was reported to have multiple funnels. The viewer was located approximately 20 miles to the southeast of the tornado.
Half dollar sized hail fell on Texas Highway 302.
Lime sized hail was found in the bar ditches on Texas State Highway 302.
The Automated Surface Observing Station at Wink (KINK) recorded several wind gusts of 60 mph. No damage was reported.

The Automated Surface Observing Station at Wink (KINK) recorded a wind gust of 67 mph. A local media outlet reported downed powerlines and trees in Kermit. The roof at the Family Activity Center of the First Baptist Church in Kermit was severely damaged.
Three power poles were knocked down by severe wind gusts. In addition, 6-8 inch diameter tree limbs were snapped.
A powper pole was reported knocked down near the Winkler/Loving county line.
A total of 7 distribution power poles were knocked down/snapped along County Road 101 just south of Wink, TX.
One distribution power pole was knocked down near the intersection of County Road 202 and State Highway 302.

Members of the Vortex2 team and TWISTEX both confirmed a rope tornado at 11:56 AM CST approximately 17 miles east southeast of Kermit, TX. The tornado then moved east northeast into western Ector County, with a confirmed dissipation time of 12:04 PM CST. There was no significant …
A thunderstorm moved over Winkler County and produced one inch hail over Kermit. A pickup truck was dented on the east side of Kermit. The cost of the damage to the truck is a rough estimate.
A cluster of thunderstorms moved across Winkler County and produced a 54 knot gust at the Wink Aiport. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 62 mph wind gust three miles northwest of Wink. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 58 mph wind gust at the Wink ASOS site. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 66 mph wind gust at the Wink ASOS.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced wind damage in Kermit. A roof was blown off of a building. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 61 mph wind gust at the Wink ASOS site.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 62 mph wind gust at the Winkler County Airport.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 62 mph wind gust near Wink.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 72 mph wind gust near Wink.

A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced wind damage in Wink. Trees were down and roofs were damaged in Wink. The power was also knocked out too. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 69 mph wind gust four miles northwest of Wink.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced tennis ball sized hail 21 miles northeast of Kermit. The hail resulted in broken skylights. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 66 mph wind gust near Wink.
A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced a 60 mph wind gust at the Winkler County Airport.

A thunderstorm moved across Winkler County and produced wind damage about two miles north of Kermit. A powerline pole was snapped which left streets on the north side of Kermit without power. Several trees were uprooted and there was damage to roofing material and metal awnings. …
A thunderstorm produced a 66 mph wind gust at the Wink ASOS site.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage in Wink, TX. The winds caused light roof damage to a church, damage to nearby power poles, and uprooted a tree. Winds were estimated to be between 70 to 80 mph. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm produced a 61 mph wind gust at the ASOS site near Wink.
A thunderstorm produced a 69 mph wind gust at the ASOS site near Wink.
A thunderstorm produced wind damage four miles east northeast of Wink. There were powerlines down on Highway 18. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage four miles east northeast of Kermit. Power lines and power poles were down along Highway 302 east of Kermit. There were some power lines also down in the City of Kermit. The time was estimated from radar. The wind speed was estimated. The cost …
A trained spotter relayed a report from his son of approximately golf ball size hail 7 miles south of Wink.
Winkler County EMC reports golf ball size hail at 113 Aiport Road in Wink.
Public reports of hail near Kermit. Hail was measured with measuring tape with several images of quarter to hen egg size hail stones. Time is estimated from radar.
A maximum wind gust of 77 mph was recorded at the Winkler County Airport ASOS (INK). The ASOS stopped reporting after this gust.
A report of ping pong ball-size hail was received from mPING.
A report of ping pong ball-size hail was received from mPING.
The sheriffs office received a report of an RV roof having been blow off onto a truck in Kermit. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages is also estimated.
